title: Scoped negative result: affine seven-cube copy floor 128 and peak tradeoff
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Adds one scoped structural negative result in `research/seven-cube-affine-seed43/`. On the smallest seven-port cube with the explicit cubic Walsh Gram, every finite affine binary factorization of the full decoder has copied-rank sum at least **128**. Two terms attain `64+64`; four attain `32+32+32+32`.

The sharp peak rank is **30**, attained by an eight-term word of total cost 240. The minimum peak among total-cost-128 decoders is **32**, so the sum and peak optima cannot be attained together. The exact total optimum under peak cap 30 remains open; 240 is an upper bound only.

Even granting every other required expense zero cost, the inherited additive stage ledger gives `D <= (s-1)*128 - s*128 = -128` for every `s>=3`. This excludes positive saving in that stated model. **No new kappa, physical supplier, selected-frontier change, or full multiplication theorem is claimed.** Non-affine masks, masked identities, different Grams, additional ports and retained information across stages are outside scope.

## Task and overlap

OS-random seed **43**, structural decoder track. Exact base: `64039f1bd3b6a523b96083fd858ad040a75e3030`. The selected PR1094 result and its actual construction/review were followed; complex remains binding, with PR589 on the bit side. Exact source blobs and SHA256 pins are in `SOURCES.json`.

`TASK.json` declares the catalogue card `complex-masked-decoder` **changed** to the donor's seven-port binary/cubic geometry question. This changes the five-cube geometry rather than rerunning its closed search. Nearest predecessors [PR1046](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1046), [PR1177](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1177), [PR1222](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1222), and [PR1482](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1482) concern the five-cube. The pending packages are overlap context, not theorem premises.

The final complete scan covered **713 open PRs and 218 discussion records**, finding only this local package for the seven-cube terms. This is bounded overlap evidence, not a novelty guarantee. Main was refreshed to `680967accfd4311f3241dc154e1f434869747b43`; all three live source blobs and the selected kappa are unchanged, with no package-path collision. No pinned sprint issue existed, so the donor's local-claim fallback was used.

## Validation

```sh
python3.12 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/seven-cube-affine-seed43
python3.12 -I -B research/seven-cube-affine-seed43/test_package.py
```

Both pass locally on **Python 3.12.13**. The primary checker uses the intersection polynomial, exact integer elimination and subset syndromes. The separate checker imports no generator/predecessor code and uses Walsh features, Fraction elimination and binary RREF.

Coverage: **65,025 ordered affine pairs in 127 exact rank orbits; 566,275 reduced source assignments; all 64 coefficient equations per assignment in the second checker; 49,152 literal witness entries per implementation**. The written rank/diagonal reduction covers arbitrary finite term counts; the finite census is not represented as formal verification of the multiplication theorem.

Ten semantic/proof-boundary controls pass. Both implementations reject rank underclaims, an omitted orbit, an omitted assignment, an omitted witness term and source corruption (**10 intended rejections**), and both pass optimized read-only relocation. Metadata/source-pin validation and `verify_selected_result.py` pass. Full selected cold replay, native/global supplier admission, physical/hosting/precision/analytic adoption, proof-assistant checking and independent human review are unrun. Hosted CI is separate.

Prepared by **Hanson Sun (@bbMisk)** with substantial **OpenAI Codex assistance** in mathematics, both implementations, verification and writing. The second implementation is by the same AI-assisted author, not independent human review. Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

The README and TASK.json describe one unclaimed next question: a fully priced arbitrary-dirty two-stage interface that retains a displayed coded total and changes the additive `s*C` charge. No such physical interface is provided, and a rank-table optimization alone cannot remove this negative deficit.
